checks.do: JIT works only when the user logs in via an IdP-initiated SSO.
SSO is enabled by default for all users, and the Default Super Administrator and Breakglass Admin can still use local credentials.
Trusted IP changes take up to 12 to 16 hours to reflect across the ZPC modules.

saml2.statement: ZPC supports SAML 2.0 for provisioning and authenticating users, so users can access ZPC directly from the IdP portal.

quotes: Zscaler Posture Control (ZPC) supports Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 for provisioning and authenticating users.
ZPC supports single-sign-on (SSO) via SAML 2.0 so that users can access ZPC directly from the IdP portal.

one-idp.statement: Only one IdP configuration can be added for a single tenant, and the Add IdP Configuration button is no longer shown once one exists; it can still be edited or deleted.

quotes: You can add only one IdP configuration for a single tenant.
After you add one IdP configuration, the Add IdP Configuration button is not visible. However, you can edit an IdP configuration or delete an IdP configuration as required.

flows.statement: The SP-initiated flow starts when the user tries to access ZPC and ZPC sends a SAML request to the IdP; in the IdP-initiated flow the user logs in from the IdP portal by clicking the ZPC application icon and the IdP sends a SAML response to ZPC's ACS URL.

quotes: The most common deployment is the SP-initiated SAML deployment where the user tries to access ZPC, which then sends a SAML request to the IdP.
In IdP-initiated SAML, a user can log in directly from an Identity Provider's portal by clicking on the ZPC application icon.
When the user clicks the ZPC application icon, the IdP generates a SAML response and sends it to ZPC's ACS URL.

jit-idp-initiated.statement: JIT provisioning works only with IdP-initiated login: ZPC needs an IdP-initiated login to retrieve user information from the IdP and does not work with SP-initiated login.

quotes: An IdP-initiated login is required for ZPC to retrieve user information from IdP and provision a user in ZPC.
JIT does not work with SP-initiated login.
JIT works only when you log in via an IDP-initiated SSO.

jit-behavior.statement: With SAML JIT provisioning, ZPC retrieves user information such as first name or role name from the SAML response, and adds a user that does not exist to the database with the role information, activated and able to access the portal.

quotes: You can enable SAML just-in-time (JIT) provisioning to allow ZPC to automatically retrieve information related to users such as first name, or role name from the SAML response.
If the user doesn't exist in the database, then the user is added to the database along with the role information. This new user is activated, and can access the ZPC Admin Portal.

jit-group-prereq.statement: Before configuring JIT provisioning, a group must exist in ZPC with the same name in the IdP and users assigned to it; this step is mandatory to avoid errors, and IdP groups take priority over ZPC groups.

quotes: Before configuring SAML JIT provisioning, make sure to first create a group in the ZPC Admin Portal, add the same group name to the IdP, and assign users to this group.
This step is mandatory to avoid any errors during configuration.
IdP groups are prioritized over ZPC groups. If a user is part of both groups, they are logged into the IdP group.

jit-multi-group.statement: If a JIT user belongs to multiple IdP groups, at least one group with the same name must exist in ZPC so the user can log in with SSO.

quotes: If the user belongs to multiple groups, then you must create at least one group with the same name in ZPC, so the user can log in to ZPC using SSO.

group-sso-name.statement: A group added for SSO must use the same name as the group on the IdP portal, and the IdP group overrides the local ZPC group.

quotes: While adding a group for SSO in the ZPC Admin Portal, make sure to use the same group name that exists on the IdP portal.
The IdP group overrides the local ZPC group.

group-sso-checkbox.statement: The Add Group window has a Single Sign-On option that lets users in the group log in to the ZPC Admin Portal directly from their IdP's portal.

quotes: Single Sign-On: Select to enable SSO. This allows users in the group to log in to the ZPC Admin Portal directly from their Identity Provider's (IdP) portal.

idp-certificate.statement: The SAML IdP certificate must be obtained from the IdP beforehand and uploaded in the ZPC Admin Portal when adding the IdP configuration, where it is used to verify the IdP's digital signature.

quotes: Before configuring the Zscaler service for SAML, ensure you obtain the SAML IdP certificate from your identity provider (IdP).
You need to upload this IdP certificate to the ZPC Admin Portal when you're adding the IdP configuration.
IdP Certificate: Upload the IdP certificate that is used to verify the digital signature of the IdP.

name-id.statement: ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format.

quotes: Name Identifier Format: ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format.

metadata.statement: The XML Metadata contains the Name Identifier Format, the Entity ID and the Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL, which is the ZPC destination URL where the SAML response must be sent by the IdP.

quotes: The XML Metadata contains the following information which you need to submit while adding an IdP configuration:
Name Identifier Format: ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format.
Entity ID: A unique identifier for a SAML entity.
Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL: ZPC destination URL where the SAML response must be sent to by the IdP.

sso-enabled-default.statement: In the IdP configuration, SSO is enabled by default for all users in the tenant; while enabled, users can log in only through SSO, and while disabled all users receive an email to reset their password and log in locally; the Default Super Administrator can use either method.

quotes: By default, SSO is enabled for all users in the specified tenant.
all users belonging to the specified tenant can log in only through SSO and they cannot log in using the local authentication method
When SSO is disabled, then all users receive an email to reset their password and log in through the local authentication method.
However, the Default Super Administrator can log in to the ZPC Admin Portal through SSO or local authentication.

breakglass.statement: If the IdP is enabled but login fails because of IdP issues, an administrator can use Sign in as Breakglass Admin on the Login page with local credentials.

quotes: If the IdP is enabled for your organization but you're not able to log in because of IdP issues, then you can log in as Breakglass Admin directly.
On the Login page, click Sign in as Breakglass Admin.
The administrator can log in using the Breakglass Admin option directly (with local credentials) even when the IdP is enabled.

auto-update-groups.statement: With Auto Update Group Based on IdP selected, user and group information is updated automatically from the IdP and the default groups (Default admin and Default Read only) associated with the user are not impacted.

quotes: Auto Update Group Based on IdP: Select to allow automatic update of user and user's group information from your IdP.
When auto update is selected, the default groups (Default admin and Default Read only) associated with the user are not impacted.

edit-delete-permission.statement: Only the Default Super Administrator can edit or delete an IdP configuration, and deleting it may result in SSO login failure.

quotes: Only the Default Super Administrator has the permission to edit or delete an IdP configuration. Deleting an IdP configuration may result in SSO login failure.

add-permission.statement: A user with admin privileges can add or manage IdP configurations, after SAML for SSO has been configured for the organization.

quotes: A user with admin privileges can add or manage IdP configurations. You must first configure SAML for SSO for your organization before proceeding with the IdP configuration.

edit-fields.statement: The Edit IdP Configuration window offers Login Name Attribute, Enable JIT and Auto Update group based on IdP, in addition to the name, issuer and SSO URL.

quotes: Name, Identity Provider Issuer: Change the name or IP issuer.
Single sign-on URL: Change the single-sing-on (SSO) URL.
Login Name Attribute: Change the login name for the IdP.
Enable JIT: Select to enable or disable just-in-time (JIT) provisioning.
Auto Update group based on IdP: Select to allow the automatic update of user and user's group information from your IdP.

idp-guides.statement: The SAML configuration page has IdP guides for Okta, PingOne, OneLogin and Azure AD, and a fifth guide for CyberArk Identity; the introductory sentence names only the first four.

quotes: Follow the relevant configuration guides of Okta, PingOne, OneLogin, and Azure AD to configure ZPC as an SP for your IdP.
- CyberArk Iadaptive
Log in to the CyberArk Identity Admin Portal.

okta-azure-nameid.statement: In the Okta and Azure AD guides, the Name ID format is set to email address and Azure's source attribute to user.mail.

quotes: Log in to Okta with admin privileges.
From the Name ID format drop-down menu, select Email Address.
Log in to the Azure AD Portal with admin privileges.
For Name identifier format, select email address from the drop-down menu.
For Source attribute, select user.mail from the drop-down menu.

onelogin-validator.statement: In the OneLogin guide the ACS (Consumer) URL Validator is https://app.us.zpccloud.net/auth/saml/acs.

quotes: Log in to OneLogin with admin privileges.
ACS(Consumer) URL Validator: Enter the following URL:
https:\/\/app.us.zpccloud.net\/auth\/saml\/acs

cyberark-nameid.statement: In the CyberArk guide the NameID Format is left at its default of Unspecified.

quotes: Log in to the CyberArk Identity Admin Portal.
NameID Format: By default, the format is Unspecified. Retain this value.

cyberark-login.statement: For CyberArk, user login names must equal the email address or SAML authentication fails; CyberArk roles function as groups.

quotes: When you create users, ensure that the Login name is the same as the email address for users.
If not, the SAML authentication fails.
Roles function as groups in the CyberArk Iadaptive.

entra-group-claim.statement: For JIT group attributes in Microsoft Entra ID, the group claim uses Cloud-only group display names, or SAMAccountName when syncing from on-premises Active Directory through Entra ID Connect, with claim name Group and namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims.

quotes: Follow these steps to configure the group attributes in:
- Microsoft Entra ID
From the Source attribute drop-down menu, select Cloud-only group display names.
If you want to sync groups and users from an on-premises Active Directory via the Microsoft Entra ID Connect sync service, then select SAMAccountName from the drop-down menu.
For Name, enter Group.
For Namespace, enter http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims.

tip-purpose.statement: ZPC excludes trusted IPs when examining publicly exposed assets or identities, which eliminates false alerts generated for those IPs.

quotes: ZPC excludes these trusted IPs when examining assets or identities that are publicly exposed and eliminates false alerts generated for IPs.

tip-super-admin-only.statement: Only the Super Admin role can access, edit or delete trusted IPs.

quotes: Only the Super Admin role can access, edit, or delete the trusted IPs.

tip-propagation-delay.statement: Trusted IP changes take up to 12 to 16 hours to reflect across the ZPC modules.

quotes: The trusted IP changes take up to 12 to 16 hours to reflect across the ZPC modules.
The trusted IP changes take up to 12 to 16 hours to reflect across the ZPC modules.

tip-upload-format.statement: A trusted IP list is entered in a downloadable template as a .csv or .xlsx file and uploaded under a list name.

quotes: Click Template to download the IP address template and enter the list of trusted IP addresses in the .csv or .xlsx file.
Drag and drop the trusted IP file or browse and upload the trusted IP file.
For Trusted IP List Name, enter a name for the trusted IP list.

tip-scope-options.statement: A trusted IP list is applied to Business Units, to Cloud Accounts (providers or individual accounts), or to All Cloud Accounts, which covers all existing and new cloud accounts.

quotes: Business Units: Select the business units from the list.
Cloud Accounts: Select the cloud service providers or individual cloud accounts from the list.
All Cloud Accounts: Select to apply the trusted IP list to all the existing and new cloud accounts.

tip-alerts-scope.statement: Selecting Alerts on the trusted IP scope step ignores all alerts on external exposure of the cloud resources associated with the trusted IP list.

quotes: select Alerts to ignore all alerts on external exposure of your cloud resources associated with the trusted IP list.

tip-delete-effect.statement: Deleting a trusted IP list updates ZPC inventories and public exposure indicators so that the associated cloud resources are viewed as publicly exposed security risks.

quotes: If you delete a trusted IP list, ZPC inventories and public exposure indicators are updated and all the associated cloud resources are viewed as publicly exposed security risks.

tip-upload-overrides.statement: Uploading a new trusted IP list file overrides the existing file and affects ZPC inventories, public exposure indicators and public exposure alerts.

quotes: Uploading a new trusted IP list file overrides the existing file and affects the ZPC inventories, public exposure indicators, and public exposure alerts.

tip-list-scope-column.statement: The Scope column of the Trusted IP Management page shows the cloud resource (All accounts, Accounts, Business Units) associated with each list.

quotes: Scope: The cloud resource (All accounts, Accounts, Business Units) associated with the trusted IP list.

idp-edit-permission.summary: The Adding IdP Configuration page says a user with admin privileges can add or manage IdP configurations, while the Editing or Deleting page says only the Default Super Administrator can edit or delete one.

positions.says: A user with admin privileges can add or manage IdP configurations.

quotes: A user with admin privileges can add or manage IdP configurations.

positions.says: Only the Default Super Administrator can edit or delete an IdP configuration.

quotes: Only the Default Super Administrator has the permission to edit or delete an IdP configuration.

idp-edit-permission.impact: Which administrators may change an existing IdP configuration is not settled by the two pages.

name-id-format.summary: The Configuring SAML SSO page says ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format, while its CyberArk steps keep the NameID Format at Unspecified.

positions.says: ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format.

quotes: Name Identifier Format: ZPC only supports email address as the Name ID format.

positions.says: In the CyberArk guide the NameID Format is retained at Unspecified.

quotes: NameID Format: By default, the format is Unspecified. Retain this value.

name-id-format.impact: Which Name ID format a given IdP must send is not settled by the page.

sso-hosts-fields.title: The ACS host for other regions and where Login Name Attribute appears
sso-hosts-fields.detail: Login Name Attribute appears on the edit page but not on the add page. The ACS host is given only for the OneLogin validator (app.us.zpccloud.net); other regions are not stated.

tip-limits.title: Trusted IP upload limits and the cause of the propagation delay
tip-limits.detail: Upload limits (rows, file size, IP or CIDR format) are not stated, and no cause is given for the 12 to 16 hour delay.
